objective: Give the mesh birth-certificate rule (Verification Charter v1.5 section 9) its mechanics: the certificate lives beside the mesh, hash-bound to it, and every workflow that lets a mesh enter a case asserts it at entry
rationale: The 2026-08-08 archive sweep (campaign/MESH_BIRTH_CERTIFICATE_AUDIT_2026-08-08.md) found 178 unique reachable meshes: 105 already certified, 47 clean-but-uncertified, and exactly one born broken -- the A3 vcoarse pyHyp mesh, which entered a case three times under reconstruction because nothing at entry asked for its certificate. The single biggest gap is structural, not individual: the mesh cache stores bare polyMesh with no quality record, so 400+ act6/act7/act9/study run dirs carry a mesh with no record beside it even though geometry_study's gate DID run checkMesh at generation -- the reading was transient (L-40: the switch that ran must be provable from the artifact). Proposed mechanics, report-only, for Infra to adopt with their own verification: (1) certificate = log.checkMesh beside the case (existing convention) plus birth_certificate.json beside every .mesh-cache entry carrying points_sha256, verdict, cells, maxAR, maxNonOrtho, maxSkew, generator, created_at. (2) Insertion points: sdk/chief_engineer/head_engineer.py save_mesh_to_cache (~line 1006) writes the certificate at cache-save; cached_mesh_available (~971) treats a cache entry without a matching-hash certificate as NOT cached, which is the charter's quarantine; restore_cached_mesh (~986) asserts hash+verdict at entry and copies the certificate into the case. sdk/chief_engineer/docker_dafoam.py mesh-cache mirror (~216-250) gets identical mechanics -- this is the pyHyp entry path, the pathology's generator. sdk/workflows/geometry_study.py persists the log its gate judged (mesh_quality_reading ~455, retry_mesh_quality ~590, rung builder ~1388-1402) into the case dir and hands it to save_mesh_to_cache. sdk/scripts/model_form_batch.py, already the exemplar (retained logs, hard gates at mesh_verdict ~569), adds assert-at-entry so an absent or unreadable log.checkMesh refuses the solver launch instead of surfacing as post-hoc exclusion. (3) Pre-registrations and docket items naming a mesh rung carry its points_sha256 plus verdict so a born-broken mesh cannot re-enter under a new case name.
cost_basis: measured; the audit's own 85 s of serial checkMesh is already spent, the mechanics themselves are code changes with no solver time
expected_knowledge_gain: Every mesh that enters an archive, a pre-registration, or a ladder rung is provably born clean at the artifact level, and a missing certificate is a refusal at entry rather than a forensic finding months later; the A3 vcoarse failure mode (same broken mesh, three case reconstructions, zero certificate checks) becomes unreachable
